question: In which of the following years was the Treaty of Bassein signed between the British East India Company and Baji Rao II, the Maratha Peshwa?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1802**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Treaty of Bassein was signed on **31 December 1802** between the British East India Company and Baji Rao II, the Maratha Peshwa.
 
• It was a significant event that marked the beginning of British dominance over the Maratha Confederacy.
 
• Under the treaty, Baji Rao II accepted the subsidiary alliance system, agreeing to maintain a **British military force** within his territory in exchange for protection.
 
• The treaty led to the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–1805), as other Maratha leaders opposed the agreement and British interference.
 
• This treaty ultimately weakened the Maratha Empire and paved the way for British expansion in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• A diplomatic strategy introduced by Lord Wellesley in 1798 to establish British dominance in India.
 
• Under this system, Indian rulers were required to accept a British military presence and pay for its maintenance, losing their autonomy in foreign affairs.
 
• The Treaty of Bassein was a classic example of the subsidiary alliance system.
 
 
 
• **Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–1805):**
 
 
• It was triggered by the Treaty of Bassein as other Maratha leaders, such as Scindia and Bhonsle, opposed British control.
 
• The British emerged victorious, significantly reducing Maratha power and influence.
 
 
 
• **Baji Rao II:**
 
 
• He was the last formal Peshwa of the Maratha Empire.
 
• His tenure was marked by internal Maratha conflicts and increasing British intervention.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Treaty:**
 
 
• The treaty marked a turning point, as it weakened the Marathas and strengthened British control over India.
 
• It set the stage for further conflicts, eventually leading to the complete dissolution of the Maratha Empire by 1818.
